flagged.evidence: The step says, “Then \(h\in C_c((0,1))\)” and that “exactly one summand is nonzero at each \(x\).” But [L4] supplies only \(g\in C_c(\mathbb R)\), while \(\eta_a\) is merely linear on \([0,a]\) and \([1-a,1]\); it need not vanish on a neighbourhood of either endpoint. Thus a permitted \(g\) nonzero arbitrarily close to 0 yields \(0\in\operatorname{supp}(h)\), so \(h\) need not lie in \(C_c((0,1))\). Independently, at every integer all terms \(h(x-m)\) vanish, contradicting “exactly one summand.” A cutoff supported strictly inside \((0,1)\), or an at-most-one-summand argument with the endpoint values handled separately, repairs the periodization conclusion.
